title: Two Israeli biologists developed a marine concrete that turns seawalls and piers into a home for sea life

trailer.text: Ido Sella and Shimrit Perkol-Finkel, Israeli entrepreneurs, met as students at Tel Aviv University, and both earned PhDs in zoology there.
According to the European Patent Office, the surface of the concrete used to build seawalls and piers is too smooth for marine life.
They set themselves a goal: to rethink concrete from the ground up.
In 2012 they founded the company ECOncrete, which produces concrete cast in moulds with ridges, pores and microstructures, so that marine organisms can latch on to it.
According to the European Patent Office, their concrete has to date been used in more than forty projects in ten countries.

paragraphs.text: Shimrit Perkol-Finkel was an Israeli marine biologist.
On her dives around the world, she was appalled by the damage done to the sea by concrete ports, breakwaters and piers.
She told ISRAEL21c that these structures destroy natural habitats and replace natural reefs with a desert of concrete.
Ido Sella told CNN that seventy percent of coastal structures worldwide are built of concrete.
According to CNN, the smooth, straight surfaces of seawalls make it difficult for algae, oysters and barnacles to latch on to them.

According to CNN, concrete can leach chemicals that turn the surrounding water more alkaline, making it hard for some marine species to survive, until the pH level of the seawater eventually returns to neutral.
According to the European Patent Office, as a result harmful or invasive species take hold in these environments and threaten local ecosystems.
According to ECOncrete, concrete is also the source of approximately 8% of CO₂ emissions worldwide.

stations.title: Two biologists, one idea, and trials at sea

paragraphs.text: Sella and Perkol-Finkel met as students at Tel Aviv University, and both loved marine life and wanted to protect it.
Perkol-Finkel said the idea was to take all the infrastructure already built and use it as a scaffold for a reef.
The founders initially tried nearly 20 concrete admixtures in the Mediterranean.

After choosing the best five, they did two years of controlled tests at several sites: in the Red Sea, in Florida, in New York and the Great Lakes, in Savannah, and at several other places in New York.
According to Globes, ECOncrete was founded in 2012 by two marine biologists: Dr. Ido Sella, the CTO, and Dr. Shimrit Perkol-Finkel, the CEO and chief scientist.
According to ISRAEL21c, the startup developed at the EISP 8200 accelerator.
According to Globes, the company received an initial investment of 400 thousand dollars from the Azouri brothers.
ECOncrete contains additives that prevent chemicals from leaching into or out of the sea.
It is cast in moulds that create ridges, pores and microstructures on the concrete surface.
According to ECOncrete, the company typically supplies both the patented admixture and the moulds.
According to CNN, tiny crevices on the surface of the blocks give larvae a place to settle and develop.
According to CNN, ridged sides and shallow pockets retain water, like a tide pool.
Prof. Tali Mass of the University of Haifa said the structure and surface of the products are favourable for microorganisms such as algae to settle, and fish then follow.
According to Sella, the organisms on the concrete surface coat it in a layer of calcium carbonate, which stops it from cracking and can increase its tensile strength tenfold.
Perkol-Finkel told Calcalist that the biological layer protects the infrastructure from corrosion and erosion and reduces the need for repairs.
According to ECOncrete, testing at WCCT showed an increase of up to 10% in compressive strength.
The concrete also stores carbon dioxide and emits less carbon than regular concrete, but the sources give different figures.

stations.title: First steps: from Haifa to Hong Kong

paragraphs.text: According to Globes, the company raised one million dollars from a small group of investors, ahead of expanding to Europe and the US in 2016.
In 2016 ECOncrete received a grant from the Israel-U.S. BIRD Foundation to work with the Besser concrete company of Michigan.
Perkol-Finkel told Globes that in Haifa the variety of species living near the company's units doubled.
Sella told CNN that the products can more than double biodiversity compared to regular concrete.
In 2018 a team led by Prof. Kenneth Leung of the University of Hong Kong installed tide pools, armor blocks and seawall panels on the Hong Kong coast.
This was done in a government-funded trial to boost biodiversity on artificial shorelines.
According to Leung, it is an attractive eco-engineering solution for dense coastal cities.

stations.title: From Jaffa Port to New York and San Diego

paragraphs.text: According to CNN, the company's products have been installed in New York, Rotterdam and Monaco.
According to the Algemeiner, the company has also installed them on shorelines in the Netherlands, New Zealand, the UK, Miami, San Francisco and Staten Island.
According to ISRAEL21c, the technology is part of the Living Breakwaters project on Staten Island, which won the Rebuild by Design competition.
According to the Algemeiner, the project at Brooklyn Bridge Park in New York helped increase the number of species in the water.
According to the Algemeiner, Harbor Island is the first area in the world to be protected by 72 interlocking blocks that enrich marine life.
The Port of San Diego embarked on a three-year pilot to install the company's products.
The Port of San Diego committed to investing $200 thousand in the company, and in exchange will be entitled to 5% in royalties on future sales of the product in the State of California.
At home too: according to Calcalist, Atarim, the Tel Aviv municipal corporation for beach development, worked with ECOncrete.
According to Calcalist, the city placed three tide pools in the waters around Jaffa Port.
Sella said that until a year and a half earlier the company had projects of 50–60 units, and now it was more than a few thousand units.
According to CNN, the company manufactures in Israel, Europe and the United States, and Sella plans to open more facilities.
According to an article in Calcalist, at the time of its publication the company employed 16 people in offices in Tel Aviv, the U.S., and Europe.
According to ISRAEL21c, the company grew in the EISP 8200 accelerator and won the accelerator's award for best startup of 2014, and by that time had raised $1.7 million in seed money.
According to Globes, it won first place in an innovation and entrepreneurship contest in Shanghai in 2015.
According to Calcalist, it won first prize at the Pitch to Rich event in 2019.
In April 2021 the company was listed among the 12 winners of the BloombergNEF pioneers list.
According to CNN, ECOncrete raised $5 million in the year before the article, including from the Bridges Israel fund and Barclays.
According to ECOncrete, the technology resulted in over 10 peer-reviewed scientific papers, but on the same page the company also states that eight such papers documented the results.
According to Calcalist, Shimrit Perkol-Finkel was killed in Tel Aviv when a truck hit her while she was riding an electric scooter.
She died in 2021.
According to Calcalist, she was 45, and is survived by her partner and three daughters.
Ido Sella continues to run the company as CEO.
ECOncrete's concrete is more expensive than regular concrete.
Sella said the cost of construction with the technology is higher than the alternative, as with any technology.
According to CNN, he also said the biological protection saves developers money in the long term.
According to ECOncrete, in one American project the technology reduced environmental mitigation penalties by approximately 80%, about $14 million.

According to an article in Global Cement, in a $75 million project to build eight breakwaters in New York State, construction with regular concrete or quarry stone would have involved an environmental mitigation cost of $18 million, and with the company's technology incorporated, the environmental benefits of the overall design and the concrete infrastructure reduce the cost to $4 million.
According to CNN, some ecologists warn that man-made structures cannot provide everything a natural shoreline provides.
Beth Strain of the University of Tasmania, who tested the products, said that wherever possible, more artificial structures should not be built.
She added that nature-based solutions require a lot of space and can take years to mature.
Leung said that in a place with strong waves and flooding, an alternative to concrete must be durable enough to meet safety regulations.

In 2015, Perkol-Finkel told Globes that there was still no regulation requiring the inclusion of the elements the company offers in the two private ports to be built in Ashdod and Haifa. In the same article, she noted that in countries with regulation on the matter, such an investment significantly reduces environmental fines and even prevents them.
An article in Frontiers in Climate stated that the efficacy and long-term sustainability of such technologies are still being researched.
The same article noted that some of its authors were employed by ECOncrete.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, חברת עתרים, תאגיד עירוני לפיתוח חופי תל אביב, שיתפה פעולה עם הסטארט-אפ הישראלי ECOncrete.
claims.quote: has partnered with Israel-based startup ECOncrete Tech Ltd., which develops eco-friendly underwater structures.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, העיר הציבה שלוש יחידות בריכות גאות במים סביב נמל יפו.
claims.quote: tide pool units in the waters surrounding the Jaffa port

claims.text: סלע אמר שעד שנה וחצי קודם לכן היו לחברה פרויקטים של 50–60 יחידות בטון, ואילו עכשיו מדובר ביותר מכמה אלפי יחידות.
claims.quote: Until one and a half years ago we had projects of 50-60 units of our concrete, now it is more than a few thousand units

claims.text: לפי CNN, החברה מייצרת את מוצריה בישראל, באירופה ובארצות הברית, וסלע מתכנן לפתוח מתקני ייצור נוספים ברחבי העולם.
claims.quote: produces its products in Israel, Europe and the United States, but Sella plans to open more manufacturing facilities around the world

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, ECOncrete מעסיקה 16 אנשים במשרדים בתל אביב, בארה"ב ובאירופה.
claims.quote: ECOncrete employs 16 people in offices in Tel Aviv, the U.S., and Europe.

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c, החברה זכתה בפרס הסטארט-אפ הטוב של 2014, ועד אז גייסה 1.7 מיליון דולר הון זרע.
claims.quote: won its award for best startup of 2014. By that time ECOncrete had raised $1.7 million in seed money

claims.text: לפי גלובס, ECOncrete זכתה במקום הראשון בתחרות החדשנות למדע וטכנולוגיה לנוער ויזמות בעולם של 2015 בשנגחאי.
claims.quote: ECOncrete recently won first place in the 2015 Entrepreneurship in the World Youth Science and Technology Innovation Contest in Shanghai.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, ECOncrete זכתה בפרס הראשון באירוע Pitch to Rich ב-2019.
claims.quote: ECOncrete won first prize at the Pitch to Rich event that took place in 2019

claims.text: לפי CNN, ECOncrete גייסה 5 מיליון דולר בשנה שקדמה לכתבה, בין היתר מקרן Bridges Israel ומברקליס.
claims.quote: which raised $5 million in funding last year, including from impact investment fund Bridges Israel and Barclays

claims.text: לפי ECOncrete, מאז 2012 הטכנולוגיה אומתה ביותר מ-40 פרויקטים ב-11 מדינות ו-8 ימים, והניבה יותר מ-10 מאמרים מדעיים שנבדקו בעמיתים.
claims.quote: in over 40 projects across 11 countries and 8 seas, resulting in over 10 peer-reviewed scientific papers.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, פרקול-פינקל נהרגה בתל אביב ביום ראשון כשנפגעה ממשאית בעת שרכבה על קורקינט חשמלי.
claims.quote: was killed in Tel Aviv on Sunday after being hit by a truck while riding an electric scooter.

claims.text: שמרית פרקול-פינקל נפטרה בתאונת דרכים ב-2021.
claims.quote: Sadly, Shimrit Perkol-Finkel passed away in a road accident in 2021.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, פרקול-פינקל הייתה בת 45 ונותרו אחריה בן זוגה ושלוש בנותיה.
claims.quote: Perkol-Finkel was 45-years-old and is survived by her partner and three daughters.

claims.text: סלע אמר שעלות הבנייה בטכנולוגיה של ECOncrete גבוהה מהחלופה, כמו בכל טכנולוגיה.
claims.quote: like any technology, the cost of construction with our technology is higher than otherwise.

claims.text: לפי CNN, החומר יקר עד 15% מבטון רגיל, אך סלע אמר שההגנה הביולוגית חוסכת למפתחים כסף בטווח הארוך.
claims.quote: Although the material is up to 15% more expensive than standard concrete, Sella said this

claims.text: לפי ECOncrete, בפרויקט אמריקאי אחד שילוב הטכנולוגיה בשוברי גלים הפחית קנסות פיצוי סביבתי בכ-80%, כ-14 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: technology in breakwaters reduced mitigation penalties by approximately 80%, or about 14 million USD.

claims.text: לפי Global Cement, בפרויקט בניו יורק שילוב הטכנולוגיה מפחית את עלות הפיצוי הסביבתי ל-4 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: the environmental benefits of the overall design and the concrete infrastructure reduce the mitigation costs to US$4m.

claims.text: לפי CNN, יש אקולוגים שמזהירים שמבנים מעשה ידי אדם אינם יכולים לשכפל את מלוא התועלות האקולוגיות של קווי חוף טבעיים.
claims.quote: But some ecologists warn that man-made structures cannot replicate the full ecological benefits of natural shorelines.

claims.text: בת' סטריין מאוניברסיטת טסמניה, שניסתה מוצרי ECOncrete, אמרה שכל אימת שאפשר כדאי להימנע מבניית מבנים מלאכותיים נוספים.
claims.quote: Wherever possible, you should try to avoid building more artificial structures,

claims.text: סטריין הוסיפה שפתרונות מבוססי טבע דורשים הרבה שטח ויכולים לקחת שנים להבשיל.
claims.quote: Strain added that nature-based solutions require a lot of space and can take years to mature.

claims.text: לאונג אמר שבאזור החשוף לגלים חזקים ולשטפונות חלופות לבטון חייבות להיות עמידות מספיק כדי לעמוד בתקנות הבטיחות.
claims.quote: adding that in a region vulnerable to strong waves and flooding, concrete alternatives must be durable enough to meet safety regulations

claims.text: פרקול-פינקל אמרה שעדיין אין רגולציה שמחייבת לכלול בפרויקטים את האלמנטים שהחברה מציעה.
claims.quote: there is still no regulation requiring the inclusion in these ventures of the elements we offer.

claims.text: במאמר ב-Frontiers צוין שהיעילות והקיימות ארוכת הטווח של טכנולוגיות 'הפיכת האפור לירוק' נתונות עדיין למחקר מתמשך.
claims.quote: the efficacy and long-term sustainability of GTG EcoTech remain subject to ongoing research

claims.text: במאמר ב-Frontiers in Climate צוין שמחבריו AL, YR ו-IS הועסקו על ידי ECOncrete Inc.
claims.quote: AL, YR, and IS were employed by ECOncrete Inc.

claims.text: לפי ECOncrete, בהשוואה לבטון מסורתי המבנים שלה תומכים בעד פי 2 מגוון ביולוגי, פי 7 אגירת פחמן ופי 16 איכות מים טובה יותר.
claims.quote: Compared to traditional concrete, ECOncrete structures support up to 2X more biodiversity, 7X more carbon storage, and 16X better water quality,

claims.text: לפי סלע, מוצרי החברה עולים 5% עד 20% יותר מבטון מסורתי, בהתאם לגודל הפרויקט.
claims.quote: products cost between 5% to 20% more than traditional concrete, depending on the size of the project.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, תערובות הבטון הימיות של ECOncrete עולות 2–7% יותר מתערובות הבטון הרגילות.
claims.quote: The environmentally friendly marine concrete mixtures offered by ECOncrete cost 2-7% more than the usual concrete mixtures

claims.text: לפי ה-Algemeiner, סלע הקים את ECOncrete יחד עם ד"ר שמרית פרקול-פינקל, שמתה באופן טראגי בתאונת קורקינט חשמלי במרץ.
claims.quote: who co-founded ECOncrete with marine biologist Dr. Shimrit Perkol-Finkel, who tragically died in an electric scooter accident in March.

claims.text: לפי הצהרת החברה, פרקול-פינקל הייתה מעורבת בתאונת דרכים ולא שרדה.
claims.quote: Yesterday afternoon, Shimrit was involved in a car accident and did not survive.
